name: Piper PA-15/17 Vagabond
variants: PA-17 Vagabond (bungee gear, dual controls, 65 hp)
summary: Small side-by-side two-seat high-wing taildragger: Piper's first postwar design, built from Cub parts with a shortened wing (the original 'short-wing Piper').

wings: High wing braced by one strut per side
Short, narrow wing, one bay shorter than a Cub's
engines: Single small flat-four in a neat cowl
fuselage: Fabric-covered tube fuselage with a tailwheel
tail: Rounded Cub-style fin and rudder and horizontal tail

tellTales: Tiny side-by-side two-seat high-wing on a tailwheel
Short, stubby wing with a strut each side
Cub-style tail on a compact fuselage

confusedWith.howToTell: The Vagabond has a shorter wing and seats two side by side; the Cub has a longer wing and tandem seating.
The Vagabond is side-by-side with a short wing; the Champ is tandem with a longer wing and cabin.
The Vagabond is smaller with a shorter wing and Cub-style tail; the Taylorcraft is larger with a longer wing and a bigger cabin.
The Vagabond has a one-bay-shorter wing and a lighter, more compact cabin; the J-4 Cub Coupe has the full Cub wing and a wider cabin.
